data.description:
## Description

**What**: Add Phase G sub-branch logic — chunk Tier 2-7 bugs into sub-branches of ≤5 each, tier-first, with file-conflict splits and a large-fix exception. Serialize sub-agent integration at the orchestrator level.

**Why**: Phase G fixes are independent per-bug and benefit from cross-fix interaction review within a small batch. The serialization prevents concurrent push races on shared sub-branch refs.

**Scope**:
- IN: Bug-batch sub-branches named `bug-batch/<debug-session-id>/tier-<N>-batch-<K>` with at most 5 bugs each; tier-first chunking preserves Phase E tier ordering; file-conflict splits within a tier produce additional sub-branches without exceeding the cap; large-fix exception (single bug whose estimated diff exceeds 500 lines) gets its own `-large`-suffixed sub-branch; **precedence rule: large-fix exception wins over file-conflict split — a >500-line bug is routed to a `-large` sub-branch and removed from any file-conflict consideration**; orchestrator-level serialization of sub-agent worktree integration into the shared sub-branch ref (no concurrent push); co-locate instructions in Phase G section header.
- OUT: Phase F logic (S4); per-sub-branch review (S6); leak detection (S9).

## Done Definitions

- When complete, /debug-everything Phase G in ci-pr mode chunks Tier 2-7 bugs into sub-branches with at most 5 bugs each, preserving tier ordering, named `bug-batch/<debug-session-id>/tier-<N>-batch-<K>`
  ← Satisfies: "Phase G chunks bugs into sub-branches with at most 5 bugs per sub-branch"
- When complete, file-conflict splits within a tier produce additional sub-branches without exceeding the 5-bug cap
  ← Satisfies: "Phase G file-conflict splits within a tier produce additional sub-branches"
- When complete, a single bug whose estimated diff exceeds 500 lines is routed to its own `-large`-suffixed sub-branch and is NOT also subject to file-conflict split logic (large-fix takes precedence)
  ← Satisfies: "Any single bug whose estimated diff exceeds 500 lines is routed to its own -large-suffixed sub-branch"
- When complete, within a Phase G batch, sub-agent integration into the shared sub-branch ref is serialized at the orchestrator level (no concurrent push) — verified by a multi-sub-agent integration test
  ← Satisfies: "Sub-agent integration into the shared sub-branch ref is serialized at the orchestrator level"
- When complete, Phase G sub-branch instructions are co-located in the Phase G section header (not cross-mode preamble)
  ← Satisfies: "Mechanism applies to Bug-Fix Mode, Phase F, Phase G with instructions co-located in each mode's section header"
- Unit tests written and passing for chunking, file-conflict split, large-fix exception precedence, and serialization
  ← Satisfies: "Phase G chunks bugs into sub-branches with at most 5 bugs"

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Orchestrator-level serialization is the sole race protection — must verify under parallel-5 dispatch with an integration test
- [Testing] Large-fix vs file-conflict precedence is a derived rule from the blue-team review — needs explicit test case

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As an operator, /debug-everything Phase G (Tier 2-7) chunks bugs into ≤5-bug sub-branches with file-conflict splits and large-fix isolation, with serialized integration to prevent race conditions
